meta.title: Enron's Stock Went From $90 To 26 Cents In 16 Months. Here's How.
meta.hook: In August 2000, Enron traded at ninety dollars a share.
meta.description: Enron used mark-to-market accounting and off-balance-sheet partnerships built by CFO Andrew Fastow to hide losses and debt for years. When the truth surfaced in October 2001, the stock collapsed from $90.75 to $0.26 within sixteen months, and the company filed for bankruptcy on December 2, 2001. Educational content only, not financial advice.

scenes.narration: In August two thousand, Enron traded at ninety dollars a share.

visual.query: corporate skyscraper glass tower low angle sunlight
visual.visual_intent: A gleaming glass corporate tower shot from a low angle against bright sky, confident, corporate power
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: the peak, hard cut. Stock price confirmed via multiple business-history sources (Britannica, KHOU).

scenes.narration: Sixteen months later, it was worth twenty-six cents.

visual.query: red stock chart crashing downward screen
visual.visual_intent: A red line chart collapsing sharply downward on a dark trading screen, stark contrast to the prior shot
visual.decision_reason: the pattern interrupt on the collapse, confirmed via Britannica/KHOU stock history

scenes.narration: Enron wasn't just a bad bet. It was built on accounting that let it book future profits today.

visual.query: financial documents spreadsheet office desk dim light
visual.visual_intent: Stacks of financial documents and a spreadsheet under a desk lamp in a dim office, secretive tone
visual.decision_reason: explains mark-to-market accounting, confirmed via Britannica/International Banker

scenes.narration: Its CFO, Andrew Fastow, built private partnerships that hid thousands of debt off Enron's own books, and pocketed tens of millions doing it.

visual.query: businessman silhouette shadow office window dark
visual.visual_intent: A single executive silhouette against a window blind, hard shadow bars across the face, thriller tone
visual.decision_reason: Fastow's off-balance-sheet SPEs ('Raptors') and ~$45M personal profit, confirmed via International Banker / Britannica

scenes.narration: In October two thousand one, Enron admitted to over six hundred million dollars in losses. The SEC opened an inquiry two days later.

visual.query: newspaper headline financial crisis close up
visual.visual_intent: A close-up of a newspaper business-section headline about corporate losses, harsh desk light
visual.decision_reason: the $638M Q3 loss disclosure and SEC inquiry, confirmed via History.com timeline / Fox News fast-facts timeline

scenes.narration: The stock never recovered. By November thirtieth, it had fallen below a dollar, and Enron filed for bankruptcy two days later.

visual.query: empty office corridor closed doors dim
visual.visual_intent: An empty, dim corporate hallway with closed office doors, stillness after collapse
visual.decision_reason: Nov 30 sub-$1 close and Dec 2 bankruptcy filing, confirmed via History.com / Fox News timeline

scenes.narration: Thousands of employees had their retirement savings tied up in that same stock. The lesson wasn't about energy trading. It was about what happens when the numbers stop meaning anything.

visual.query: cardboard box desk items office layoff
visual.visual_intent: A cardboard box of personal desk items on an empty desk, quiet aftermath, warm low light
visual.decision_reason: closing beat on the human cost and the systemic lesson, widely reported consequence of the collapse
